text.p: Here are highlights from Polish newspapers this morning.

- The treasury ministry will hand over its 46.6 percent stake in the ailing Gdynia shipyard to the Szczecin shipyard under a plan to set up a shipbuilding group in Poland, the ministry said. Under the scheme the state-owned Bank Handlowy will sell its 18.6 percent equity in Gdynia to the Szczecin yard.

- The Szczecin yard, PZM shipping firm and the Pomorski Bank Kredytowy (PBKS) in Szczecin have signed a letter of intent on building ships for PZM in the bankrupt Gdansk yard. The letter was preseted to the the yard's receiver.

- The Polish unit of General Motors has won a tax case against the country's tax office in the Supreme Administrative Court (NSA). The office had not wanted to accept GM's downward correction of the owed value added added tax in 1995 amounting to 181,200 zlotys.

- Economic ministries' officials from Poland and Bulgaria have began talks on settling Sofia's debt dating back to the communist era. Poland says it will liberalise trade with Bulgaria only after it repays its debt of 105 million trasferable rubles and $100 million.

- Merrill Lynch and Robert Fleming investment banks will co-manage the consortium that will offer shares of the KGHM Polska Miedz copper combine, the privatisation of which will start this year, the Union Bank of Switzerland (UBS) official Rafal Sosna said.

- Trade exchange between Poland and China reached $289.9, which accounted for 0.37 percent of China's total exports and 0.03 percent of imports and 0.19 percent of Poland's exports and 1.5 percent of imports, Poland's foreign trade ministry said.

- The Era GSM digital mobile phone operator, controlled by Polska Telefonia Cyfrowa (PTC), will invest two billion zlotys by the end of 1998 in equipment provided by Ericsson and Siemens, which will allow the operator to cover 65 percent of Poland, PTC's president Tadeusz Kubiak said.

- General Motors Poland (GMP) has confirmed that the listed Mostostal Zabrze construction firm will build its car assembly plant in the southern city of Gliwice worth 90 million marks, GMP's official Jaroslaw Dabek said.
- The Shell Oil will sell chemical products of Poland's Organika firm in Western Europe under a recently signed agreement.
- Nomura investment bank recommended holding stocks of Mostostal Zabrze construction firm and Stomil Sanok tyre maker in its March report.
